Rashi on Shabbat 145b:10:1.hebrew: מפני מה עופות שבבבל שמנים - משל א"י:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:10:1.english: Why are the fowl in Babylonia fat - [Fatter] than those of the Land of Israel.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:10:2.hebrew: כלך - לכה לך, אלא שקיצר הלשון:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:10:2.english: Go [kelakh] - [That is,] "go for yourself" [lekhah lekha], except that he shortened the expression.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:10:3.english: To the desert of Gaza - And it is [part] of the Land of Israel.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:10:4.hebrew: מועדים שבבבל שמחים - רגילים לשמוח במועדים יותר מא"י:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:10:4.english: Festivals in Babylonia are joyous - [They are] accustomed to rejoice on the Festivals more than [in] the Land of Israel.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:10:5.hebrew: מפני שהם עניים - וכל השנה אין להם שמחה במאכל ומשתה, ואין להם מרגוע ממלאכה; לפיכך במועדים כל שמחתם:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:10:5.english: Because they are poor - And all year they have no joy in food and drink, and they have no rest from labor; therefore, on the Festivals [is] all their joy.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:10:6.english: Distinguished - They distinguish themselves with fine garments.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:10:8.hebrew: שאינן בני תורה - כל כך לכבדם כבני ארץ ישראל מחמת תורתם, מכבדים אותם מחמת לבושיהן שנראין חשובים:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:10:8.english: That they are not Torah scholars - so much [so] as to honor them like the people of Eretz Yisrael on account of their Torah; [rather,] they honor them on account of their garments, [through which] they appear important.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:11:1.english: Children - Young men who have not reached [the level of] logical reasoning.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:11:2.hebrew: מפני שלא גלו - העופות כמו אותן של א"י, כדאמרינן לקמן:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:11:2.english: Because they were not exiled - [Meaning] the fowl [were not exiled] like those of the Land of Israel, as we say later.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:11:3.hebrew: שאנן מואב מנעוריו וגו' - סיפיה דקרא "על כן עמד טעמו בו", אלמא הגולין מפיגין טעמן ושמנן:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:11:3.english: Moab has been at ease since his youth, etc. - The end of the verse [states]: "therefore his taste remained in him"; thus [we see that] those who are exiled lose their flavor and their fatness.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:12:1.hebrew: נ"ב שנה - משגלו בימי צדקיה בחרבות ירושלים עד שנפקדו בימי כורש, ואז עלו מהם לייסד את הבית, י"ח שנים קודם גמר הבנין, שהיא לסוף ע' שנה בשנת שתים לדריוש, כדאמרי' במגילה (דף יא:):
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:12:1.english: Fifty-two years - From when they were exiled in the days of Zedekiah at the destruction of Jerusalem until they were remembered in the days of Cyrus, and then [some] of them went up to lay the foundation of the Temple, eighteen years before the completion of the building, which was at the end of seventy years, in the second year of Darius, as we say in Megillah (11b).

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:13:1.hebrew: וכולן חזרו - הבהמות ועופות ואף הדגים, חוץ מן קולייס האספנין. וכולן חזרו, דהא "עד בהמה" כתיב, ומכלל דמכאן ואילך הדור, חוץ מקולייס כדמפרש:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:13:1.english: And they all returned - The beasts, birds, and even the fish, except for the kolyas ha’ispanin. And they all returned, for it is written “until behemah [beast],” [which] implies that from then onward they returned, except for the kolyas, as [the Gemara] explains.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:13:2.hebrew: הני מדרי דבבל מהדרי מיא לעין עיטם - מדרונות שבבבל מחזירין מים הנשפכים בהן לעין עיטם, שהוא מקום גבוה שבא"י, שאותו מעיין מביא מים לבית טבילת כה"ג ביה"כ, דמתוקן בחומת עזרה על גבי שער המים, כדאמרינן בסדר יומא (דף לא.): עין עיטם גבוה מקרקע העזרה כ"ג אמות. והיאך מחזירין? שיש בפרת סילונות וסולמות למטה מן הקרקע (הים), ודרך אותן סולמות חוזרין המים לא"י, וחוזרין ונובעין במעיינות. והדגים חזרו דרך אותן סולמות, שנוחים להעלותן יותר מדרך פרת עצמו:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:13:2.english: Those inclines of Babylonia return the water to the spring of Eitam - The slopes in Babylonia return the water that is poured into them to the spring of Eitam, which is a high place in the Land of Israel, for that spring brings water to the immersion chamber of the High Priest on Yom Kippur, which was installed in the wall of the [Temple] Courtyard above the Water Gate, as we say in Seder Yoma (31a): "The spring of Eitam is twenty-three cubits higher than the floor of the [Temple] Courtyard." And how do they return [the water]? For in the Euphrates there are conduits and stepped channels beneath the ground (the sea), and through those channels the water returns to the Land of Israel and wells up again in the springs. And the fish returned through those channels, for they are easier to ascend than [swimming] by way of the Euphrates itself.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:13:4.english: Because its spine is not strong - Its spine is not hard.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:14:2.english: Tzippori and Tiberias [are] from Eretz Yisrael:

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:14:3.hebrew: לטבריה - לבוז ולהטיל עליהם עול, ולא שמתכוונין לבטלן משמחת הרגל, אבל הקללה גרמה לכך:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:14:3.english: To Tiberias - To plunder and to impose a yoke upon them. And [it is] not that they intend to keep them from the joy of the Festival, rather the curse caused this.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:14:4.english: Komtin - [It] is a foreign word, [meaning] a ruler.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:15:1.hebrew: שאינן במקומם - שמא"י גלו לשם, והגולה למקום נכרי מציין עצמו במלבושים שיהא חשוב:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:15:1.english: That they are not in their place - For they were exiled there from the Land of Israel, and one who is exiled to a foreign place distinguishes himself with garments so that he will be esteemed.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:15:2.english: In [my] town, my name - In my city, I do not need to be honored except by my name, by which I am recognized.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:15:3.english: In [a place that is] not [my] city - In a place that is not my city.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:15:4.hebrew: תותבאי - כבודי תלוי בשמלתי. שמלתו מתרגמינן תותביה (שמות כב, כה):
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:15:4.english: Totevai - My honor depends on my garment. "His garment" is translated [into Aramaic as] "totevei" (Exodus 22:25).

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:15:5.hebrew: הבאים - אותן של יעקב שיבאו לבבל, ישרשו ויעשו ציצין ופרחים לתורה. וסייעתא אתיא לר' יוחנן, דטעמא דמצויינין לאו לפי שאינן בני תורה כדרבי אסי, אלא לפי שאינן במקומן:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:15:5.english: Those who come - [Meaning] those [descendants] of Jacob who will come to Babylonia will take root and produce buds and blossoms for the Torah. And [this] comes as support for Rabbi Yochanan, that the reason they are distinguished [by special dress] is not because they are not Torah scholars, as Rabbi Asi [said], but rather because they are not in their [own] place.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:1:1.hebrew: לעדות אשה - לומר לאשה מת בעליך, דאקילו בה רבנן משום עיגונא. וכל דמקדש אדעתא דרבנן מקדש, ואפקועי רבנן לקדושין מיניה:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:1:1.english: For testimony [regarding] a woman - To say to a woman, "Your husband died," for the Sages were lenient in her [case] because of [the concern of] *igun* [being stranded in marriage]. And anyone who betroths [a woman] betroths [her] in accordance with the will of the Sages, and the Sages annul the betrothal from him.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:2:1.hebrew: לעדות בכור - בכור ביד כהן, כשנתנו ישראל לו שלם ואירע לו בו מום, קי"ל בבכורות (דף לה.): נחשדו כהנים להטיל מום בבכור, ואין נאמן לומר "מום זה נפל בו מאיליו", וצריך להביא עדים. ואמרינן התם דאשה כשרה לעדות זו:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:2:1.english: For testimony [regarding] a firstborn - [When there is] a firstborn [animal] in the possession of a priest, where an Israelite gave it to him unblemished and a blemish occurred in it, we hold in Bekhorot (35a) [that] priests are suspected of inflicting a blemish on a firstborn, and [therefore the priest] is not believed to say, "This blemish occurred in it on its own," and he must bring witnesses. And we say there that a woman is eligible for this testimony.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:3:1.english: Say: for testimony for which a woman is valid - And for this [case] too, she is valid.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:5:1.hebrew: גברא יתירא - ר"ש, דמתני' ר"א תנן בה:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:5:1.english: An additional person - [Namely,] Rabbi Shimon, for in our Mishnah we learned [it in the name of] Rabbi Elazar.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:5:2.hebrew: אתא לאשמעינן - בתמיה, כלומר: מה בא ללמדנו אם לא זאת:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:5:2.english: He came to teach us - [This is said] as a question, meaning: what did he come to teach us if not this?

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:6:1.english: Anything that was placed in hot water - That is to say, it was cooked.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:6:2.english: One may soak it in hot water - In order that it be dissolved.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:6:3.hebrew: וכל שלא בא בחמין - כגון בשר יבש שאוכלין אותו חי ע"י הדחק:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:6:3.english: And anything that was not placed in hot water - Such as dried meat, which is eaten raw with difficulty.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:6:4.hebrew: מדיחין אותו - ולא אמרי' זהו בישוליה, אבל לא שורין:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:6:4.english: One may rinse it - And we do not say [that] this is its cooking, but one may not soak [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:6:5.english: Except for the old salted [fish] - Salted fish from last year.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:6:6.hebrew: וקולייס האיספנין - שם דג שאוכלין אותו מחמת מלחו ע"י הדחה בחמין. והנך, אפילו הדחה נמי לא, שזהו גמר מלאכתן והוי בשול:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:6:6.english: And kolyas ha'ispanin - [This is] the name of a fish that is eaten, on account of its saltiness, by means of rinsing in hot water. And [as for] these, even rinsing is also not [permitted], for this is the completion of their preparation and it constitutes cooking.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:7:1.english: In what case - is [it] "that which came into hot water," that they go back and soak it in hot water?

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:7:2.hebrew: תרנגולתיה דר' אבא - מבשלה ושורה אותה ימים רבים בחמין למחות מאליה, ואוכלה לרפואה:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:7:2.english: The chicken of Rabbi Abba - He cooks it and soaks it for many days in hot water to dissolve on its own, and eats it for healing.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:7:3.hebrew: בר תלתא טרפי - בן ג' שנים:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:7:3.english: [Wine] of three leaves - Three years old.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:7:4.english: I would have been forced - I would have been forced to vomit out of disgust.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:8:1.hebrew: רייק - רוקק מכותחא דבבלאי כשזוכרו, שהיה מאוס בעיניו:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:8:1.english: Would spit - [He] spits from Babylonian kutach when he remembers it, for it was disgusting in his eyes.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:8:2.hebrew: אמר רב יוסף כו' - קשה היה בעיניו שנמאסין בני בבל על בני ארץ ישראל. אמר: אנו נמי יש לנו לרוק מתרנגולתיה דר' אבא שהם אוכלים:
Rashi on Shabbat 145b:8:2.english: Rav Yosef said, etc. - It was distressing in his eyes that the Babylonians were repulsive to the people of the Land of Israel. He said: We also have [reason] to spit from Rabbi Abba's chicken that they eat.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:8:3.english: And furthermore, kutaḥ - [It] is not so disgusting in the eyes of the rest of the people of the West [Eretz Yisrael].

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:8:4.english: For Rav Gaza said, etc. - And they requested that kutach from him.

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:9:1.english: [If] one rinsed - kolyas [ha'ispanin], what [is the law]?

Rashi on Shabbat 145b:9:2.english: [He is] liable [to bring] a sin-offering - For it is cooking.

Tosafot on Shabbat 145b:12:1.hebrew: בהמה בגימטריא - אסמכתא בעלמא היא, דנ"ב נפקא לן בלאו גימטריא, כדפי' בקונטרס:
Tosafot on Shabbat 145b:12:1.english: Behema in gematria - This is merely a scriptural allusion [asmakhta], for fifty-two [years] is derived without gematria, as Rashi explained.
